visual.general_description: Frontal infant chest and abdomen radiograph with thin line-like devices and printed exposure and weight text.
visual.detailed_description: Black-and-white frontal radiograph of an infant chest and abdomen in portrait orientation; ribs, spine, pelvis and upper femora are visible. Printed text in the upper right corner reads "62kV 1.6mAs 1.2ffd" on one line, "29WKS" on the next and "1240g" below it. The upper left corner shows bright, over-exposed equipment shapes near the head and neck; no legible text is visible there. No left or right side marker is legible. A thin straight radio-opaque line runs obliquely from the upper neck region down the midline of the chest and ends in the lower chest above the stomach gas; a shorter, thinner line ends in the upper chest. A pair of closely parallel thin radio-opaque lines runs vertically in the midline through the upper and mid abdomen, then curves toward the image right in the lower abdomen and leaves the field at the right edge. Round and oval soft-tissue discs lie at the image-left lateral margin beside the lower chest and the abdomen. A large gas-filled rounded lucency lies in the image-right upper abdomen, with multiple gas-filled bowel loops across the abdomen; lung fields are aerated with a thin rib cage.

visual.general_description: Twelve-lead ECG printout with a printed measurement header showing a rapid regular narrow-complex rhythm.
visual.detailed_description: A header block at the top lists Rate 259, PR with no value, QRSD 67, QT 146, QTc 303, then AXIS with P with no value, QRS 119 and T 268. A twelve-lead tracing on pink millimetre grid paper is arranged in three rows and four columns; small lead labels read I, aVR, V1 and V4 in the first row, II, aVL, V2 and V5 in the second row and III, aVF, V3 and V6 in the third row. Regular, closely spaced narrow QRS complexes run across every lead, about ten to twelve complexes per lead segment; polarity and amplitude differ between leads. The footer prints "Speed: 25 mm/sec", "Limb: 10 mm/mV", "Chest: 10 mm/mV", a boxed "50% 0.05-150 Hz", a zero-filled location field and a Philips logo; a few further characters at the right end are unreadable.

panels.general_description: Frontal infant chest and abdomen radiograph with several thin line-like devices and printed text.
panels.detailed_description: Frontal black-and-white radiograph of an infant chest and abdomen with the printed panel letter "(a)" below it. Printed text at the upper right reads "L", "NICU" and "2 days / 1240g"; text at the lower right reads "62kV 1.6mAs 120ffd". A thin radio-opaque line descends from the upper midline of the neck through the chest and curves toward the image right in the lower chest and upper abdomen, ending near a rounded gas density in the image-right upper abdomen. A straight bright line in the lower chest and upper abdomen runs obliquely toward the image-left lower margin with its upper end near the level of the diaphragm. A paired line runs down the midline of the abdomen from about the diaphragm level, curves toward the image right in the lower abdomen and continues along the right margin. Round and oval soft-tissue discs lie at the image-left chest margin and the image-right flank; gas-filled bowel loops fill the abdomen.

panels.general_description: Lateral infant chest and abdomen radiograph with two thin line-like devices and printed text.
panels.detailed_description: Lateral black-and-white radiograph of an infant chest and abdomen with the spine along the image left and the printed panel letter "(b)" below it. Printed text at the upper right reads "NICU" and "2 days / 1240g", with a partly cut-off letter above it. One thin radio-opaque line descends in a smooth curve from the top edge through the chest in front of the spine and ends in the upper abdomen in the lower third of the image. A second thin line has its upper end in the lower part of the chest, curves forward and downward through the abdomen and reaches a small hub-like density at the image-right edge, beyond which thin parallel lines continue. A round disc density lies in the mid chest toward the image right and an oval disc lies at the anterior abdomen; gas-filled bowel loops fill the abdomen.
